claims: The exact origins of April Fools' Day are unknown.
April Fools' Day has been celebrated for centuries.
A popular theory suggests that France switched from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar in the 1560s.
A popular theory suggests that those who continued to celebrate the New Year in late March instead of January 1 were called "April fools".
A popular theory suggests that those who continued to celebrate the New Year in late March instead of January 1 had pranks played on them.
The Roman festival of Hilaria was held at the end of March.
The Roman festival of Hilaria celebrated the resurrection of Attis.
In France, the April Fools' Day tradition involves pinning paper fish to people's backs.
In France, the April Fools' Day tradition refers to people as an "April fish" (poisson d'avril).
April Fools' Day is traditionally called Gowkie Day in Scotland.
Gowkie Day is named after the gowk (cuckoo bird).
The gowk (cuckoo bird) is a symbol of a fool.
